correctness.rationale: In each strict coordinate-order chamber median T equals a selector S with S1=1. Telescoping f differences into edge steps H_k shows its weighted BV seminorm operator norm equals max_k V_w(SH_k)/w_k. Locality restricts a step-column change to edges k−1,k,k+1, or boundary pairs; constructed strict-order neighborhoods realize each listed extremum, with nearby input f+εH_k attaining the local induced norm. Integrating along line segments across finite chambers extends sharp upper bound globally, including ties by continuity. Thus L_n=max{1,w₂/w₁,w_{m−1}/w_m,max interior (w_{k−1}+w_k+w_{k+1})/w_k}, m=n−1, and n=2 gives identity. Irreducible tridiagonal A_m has unique positive Perron vector w_i=sin((i−1/2)π/m), eigenvalue 1+2cos(π/m), so Collatz–Wielandt gives the unique up-to-scale optimum. For n=4, f=(0,2,1,3), g=f+ε(0,0,1,1), unit weights, exact output-difference amplification factor 3. Independently enumerated all order chambers n=2..6 and three positive weight vectors with rational column norms; all agree. Finite chambers prove only those sizes; analytic argument covers all n.
